data.narrative:
Fervo Energy, a geothermal power technology company founded by Tim Latimer and Jack Norbeck, is approaching an IPO after raising over $1.5 billion in private capital. The valuation benchmark universe spans the Climate & Energy sector, which contains 9 public and private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen, alongside one public comparable (LNZA).

The peer-median approach is not applicable to this analysis. Despite nine climate and energy sector peers existing, the filtering criteria—same stage, adjacent stage, and similar valuation tier—yielded insufficient datapoints (fewer than three) to support a credible median calculation. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias given the heterogeneity of business models, capital intensity, and commercialization timelines within climate tech. No other triangulation methods produced sufficient quantitative support from the available dataset.

The absence of reliable peer multiples or comparable transaction data at Fervo's stage and scale means this valuation exercise cannot be anchored to conventional DCF or trading-multiple frameworks with confidence. Key uncertainties include the appropriate risk discount for pre-revenue infrastructure deployment, the timing and magnitude of cash generation, and whether public market appetite for frontier geothermal technology will sustain IPO valuations. A defensible range requires either narrower peer identification or forward-looking project-level cash flow modeling—neither of which the current dataset supports.
